locator: Hand Hygiene DETAILED §1 BEFORE touching a patient
quote:
BEFORE touching a patient
Any time you approach and will touch a patient — including to take a pulse, adjust a pillow, assist with
positioning, or any other direct patient contact. Protects the patient from pathogens on your hands.
title: BEFORE touching a patient

locator: Hand Hygiene DETAILED §2 BEFORE a clean or aseptic procedure
quote:
BEFORE a clean or aseptic procedure
Before any invasive procedure, sterile technique, or contact with a non-intact skin site. Examples: inserting
IV/urinary catheter, wound care, oral care, medication preparation at bedside, handling sterile equipment.
Perform hand hygiene immediately before donning sterile gloves.
title: BEFORE a clean or aseptic procedure

locator: Hand Hygiene DETAILED §3 AFTER body fluid exposure risk
quote:
AFTER body fluid exposure risk
After contact with blood, body fluids, secretions, excretions, mucous membranes, non-intact skin, wound
dressings, or any object that may be contaminated. Perform even if gloves were worn. Protects you and the
environment from patient pathogens.
title: AFTER body fluid exposure risk

locator: Hand Hygiene DETAILED §4 AFTER touching a patient
quote:
AFTER touching a patient
After any direct patient contact — even if the contact seemed clean. After helping the patient drink, after a
handshake, after adjusting a patient's call light. Protects the environment and other patients.
title: AFTER touching a patient

locator: Hand Hygiene DETAILED §5 AFTER touching patient surroundings
quote:
AFTER touching patient surroundings
After touching any object or furniture in the immediate patient environment — even if the patient was not
touched. Examples: bed rails, call light, bedside table, IV pump, vital signs equipment, door handle inside
patient room. Protects you and others from environmental pathogens.

PRODUCT SELECTION: ABHR vs. SOAP AND WATER
Alcohol-Based Hand Rub (ABHR) is the preferred method for hand hygiene in most clinical situations due to superior
antimicrobial efficacy, faster action, less skin damage, and greater convenience. Soap and water is required in
specific clinical situations.
Product/Method
When to Use
ABHR Preferred (all other situations)
Routine patient care in the absence of visible soiling
Before and after patient contact (Moments 1, 4, 5)
After removing gloves
Before and after eating (if hands not visibly soiled)
Soap & Water REQUIRED
Hands visibly soiled with blood, body fluids, or dirt
After using the restroom
Known or suspected Clostridioides difficile (C. diff) exposure — spores not
killed by ABHR
Known or suspected norovirus or other non-enveloped virus outbreaks
After contact with a patient with known Bacillus anthracis infection
Soap & Water Preferred
Before eating and handling food
After potential exposure to spore-forming organisms in outbreak settings
title: AFTER touching patient surroundings

locator: Hand Hygiene DETAILED §1 Apply Product
quote:
Apply Product
Dispense sufficient ABHR to cover all hand surfaces (approximately 1–3 mL or 2–3 pump actuations). If
hands feel dry after rubbing, you did not use enough product.
title: Apply Product

locator: Hand Hygiene DETAILED §2 Palm to Palm
quote:
Palm to Palm
Rub palms together vigorously in a circular motion until product is distributed across both palms.
title: Palm to Palm

locator: Hand Hygiene DETAILED §3 Palm Over Dorsum
quote:
Palm Over Dorsum
Right palm over left dorsum with interlaced fingers; rub. Repeat with left palm over right dorsum.
title: Palm Over Dorsum

locator: Hand Hygiene DETAILED §4 Palm to Palm with Interlaced Fingers
quote:
Palm to Palm with Interlaced Fingers
Rub palm to palm with fingers interlaced to clean between and around fingers.
title: Palm to Palm with Interlaced Fingers

locator: Hand Hygiene DETAILED §5 Backs of Fingers (Rotational)
quote:
Backs of Fingers (Rotational)
Rub backs of fingers against opposing palms with fingers interlocked (cupped hands).
title: Backs of Fingers (Rotational)

locator: Hand Hygiene DETAILED §6 Rotational Rubbing of Thumbs
quote:
Rotational Rubbing of Thumbs
Rotational rubbing of left thumb clasped in right palm and vice versa. Thumbs are frequently missed.
title: Rotational Rubbing of Thumbs

locator: Hand Hygiene DETAILED §7 Rotational Rubbing of Fingertips
quote:
Rotational Rubbing of Fingertips
Rotational rubbing of clasped fingers of right hand in left palm and vice versa. Clean under fingernails.
title: Rotational Rubbing of Fingertips

locator: Hand Hygiene DETAILED §8 Allow to Dry Completely
quote:
Allow to Dry Completely
Rub hands until product has completely evaporated and hands are dry. Do NOT wipe hands on clothing or
paper towel to speed drying — this reduces efficacy.
title: Allow to Dry Completely

locator: Hand Hygiene DETAILED §1 Wet Hands
quote:
Wet Hands
Wet hands with clean running water (warm preferred, not hot). Avoid splashing. Turn faucet on with paper
towel if foot/elbow controls unavailable.
title: Wet Hands

locator: Hand Hygiene DETAILED §2 Apply Soap
quote:
Apply Soap
Apply sufficient soap to cover all hand surfaces. Antibacterial soap is not required and not preferred over plain
soap for routine hand hygiene.
title: Apply Soap

locator: Hand Hygiene DETAILED §3 Lather and Scrub — 20 Seconds Minimum
quote:
Lather and Scrub — 20 Seconds Minimum
Lather hands vigorously and scrub all surfaces using the same seven-step WHO technique as described for
ABHR above (palm to palm, dorsa, interlaced, backs of fingers, thumbs, fingertips).
title: Lather and Scrub — 20 Seconds Minimum

locator: Hand Hygiene DETAILED §4 Rinse Thoroughly
quote:
Rinse Thoroughly
Rinse hands under running water. Ensure all soap is removed. Hold hands lower than wrists and elbows to
prevent contamination of clean hands.
title: Rinse Thoroughly

locator: Hand Hygiene DETAILED §5 Dry with Single-Use Towel
quote:
Dry with Single-Use Towel
Dry hands thoroughly with a clean, single-use paper towel using a patting motion. Do not rub vigorously as
this damages skin and may increase bacterial shedding.
title: Dry with Single-Use Towel

locator: Hand Hygiene DETAILED §6 Turn Off Faucet
quote:
Turn Off Faucet
Use a fresh dry paper towel to turn off the faucet. Do not re-contaminate clean hands by touching the faucet
handle directly.
title: Turn Off Faucet

locator: Hand Hygiene DETAILED §7 Discard Towel Without Touching Waste Bin
quote:
Discard Towel Without Touching Waste Bin
Use the paper towel to open the waste bin lid if needed, then discard. Use towel to open the door if room door
has a handle rather than a push plate.
title: Discard Towel Without Touching Waste Bin

locator: Infection Control and Prevention §1 Hand Hygiene Protocol
quote:
Hand Hygiene Protocol
All clinical staff must perform hand hygiene using WHO-approved technique with alcohol-based hand rub or soap
and water before and after patient contact, after contact with potentially infectious material, and before
donning/after removing gloves.
title: Hand Hygiene Protocol

locator: Infection Control and Prevention §2 Personal Protective Equipment (PPE)
quote:
Personal Protective Equipment (PPE)
Staff must select and use appropriate PPE based on transmission-based precautions. This includes gloves,
gowns, masks/respirators, and eye protection. PPE must be properly donned, doffed, and disposed of per
established protocol.
title: Personal Protective Equipment (PPE)

locator: Infection Control and Prevention §3 Sterilization & Disinfection
quote:
Sterilization & Disinfection
All reusable medical equipment must be properly decontaminated, cleaned, and sterilized or high-level disinfected
according to manufacturer instructions and facility protocols before use on another patient.
title: Sterilization & Disinfection

locator: Infection Control and Prevention §4 Surveillance & Reporting
quote:
Surveillance & Reporting
Ongoing surveillance of HAIs must be conducted. Reportable conditions must be submitted to appropriate public
health authorities within required timeframes.
title: Surveillance & Reporting

locator: Infection Control and Prevention §5 Isolation Procedures
quote:
Isolation Procedures
Contact, droplet, and airborne precautions must be implemented appropriately. Signage, dedicated equipment,
and private rooms (when available) must be utilized.
title: Isolation Procedures

locator: Patient Rights  Care in a Safe Setting §1 Safe Environment Standards
quote:
Safe Environment Standards
The physical environment must be free from hazards that could cause patient harm. This includes proper
maintenance, adequate lighting, secure fixtures, and removal of environmental risks.
title: Safe Environment Standards

locator: Patient Rights  Care in a Safe Setting §2 Staff Conduct & Training
quote:
Staff Conduct & Training
All staff, volunteers, and contractors must receive training on patient rights, professional boundaries, and
prohibited behaviors. Zero-tolerance policies for abuse must be enforced.
title: Staff Conduct & Training

locator: Patient Rights  Care in a Safe Setting §3 Incident Reporting
quote:
Incident Reporting
All incidents, near-misses, and potential safety concerns must be reported through established channels.
Retaliation against staff who report concerns in good faith is prohibited.
title: Incident Reporting

locator: Patient Rights  Care in a Safe Setting §4 Monitoring & Oversight
quote:
Monitoring & Oversight
Hospitals must have systems to monitor patient safety, including surveillance in appropriate areas, regular safety
rounds, and mechanisms for patients to report concerns anonymously.
title: Monitoring & Oversight

locator: Patient Rights  Care in a Safe Setting §5 Response Protocols
quote:
Response Protocols
Clearly defined protocols must exist for responding to safety incidents, including immediate patient protection,
notification of appropriate parties, investigation, and corrective action.
title: Response Protocols

locator: Medical Screening Exam (EMTALA) §1 Medical Screening Examination
quote:
Medical Screening Examination
A qualified medical professional must perform an MSE on every individual who presents to the ED or hospital
property requesting examination or treatment for a medical condition. The MSE must be the same regardless of
payment status.
title: Medical Screening Examination

locator: Medical Screening Exam (EMTALA) §2 Stabilization Requirement
quote:
Stabilization Requirement
If an Emergency Medical Condition (EMC) is identified, the hospital must provide stabilizing treatment within its
capabilities before transferring or discharging the patient.
title: Stabilization Requirement

locator: Medical Screening Exam (EMTALA) §3 Transfer Protocols
quote:
Transfer Protocols
Transfers of unstabilized patients may only occur if: the patient requests transfer, a physician certifies benefits
outweigh risks, and the receiving facility has accepted the patient and has appropriate capabilities.
title: Transfer Protocols

locator: Medical Screening Exam (EMTALA) §4 On-Call Physician Responsibilities
quote:
On-Call Physician Responsibilities
Hospitals must maintain on-call lists and ensure on-call specialists respond to EMTALA obligations within a
reasonable time when called to provide stabilizing care.
title: On-Call Physician Responsibilities

locator: Medical Screening Exam (EMTALA) §5 Anti-Dumping Provisions
quote:
Anti-Dumping Provisions
No hospital may delay MSE or stabilizing treatment to inquire about insurance status or payment ability. Financial
screening may not occur prior to clinical screening.
title: Anti-Dumping Provisions

locator: Informed Consent §1 Disclosure Requirements
quote:
Disclosure Requirements
Providers must disclose: the diagnosis, proposed treatment/procedure, material risks and benefits, alternatives to
proposed treatment, risks of non-treatment, and the identity of practitioners who will perform the procedure.
title: Disclosure Requirements

locator: Informed Consent §2 Capacity Assessment
quote:
Capacity Assessment
The consenting individual must have decisional capacity. When capacity is in question, a formal assessment must
be documented. For patients lacking capacity, the legally authorized representative must provide consent.
title: Capacity Assessment

locator: Informed Consent §3 Documentation Standards
quote:
Documentation Standards
The signed consent form must be present in the medical record before elective procedures. The form must
include: date, time, specific procedure, practitioner name, patient/representative signature, and witness signature.
title: Documentation Standards

locator: Informed Consent §4 Special Consent Situations
quote:
Special Consent Situations
Separate consents are required for: blood transfusions, HIV testing, release of records, research participation,
photography, and treatment of minors (with appropriate exceptions for emergencies).
title: Special Consent Situations

locator: Informed Consent §5 Right to Refuse
quote:
Right to Refuse
Competent patients have the absolute right to refuse any treatment. Refusal must be documented, including
patient education about risks of refusal and the patient's stated reasons.
title: Right to Refuse

locator: Medication Administration §1 The Five Rights (Minimum Standard)
quote:
The Five Rights (Minimum Standard)
Before administering any medication, staff must verify: Right Patient (two patient identifiers), Right Drug, Right
Dose, Right Route, and Right Time. Many facilities have expanded to seven or ten rights.
title: The Five Rights (Minimum Standard)

locator: Medication Administration §2 Medication Reconciliation
quote:
Medication Reconciliation
A complete and accurate medication list must be obtained at admission, reconciled at each transition of care, and
provided to the patient/caregiver at discharge. Discrepancies must be resolved by a licensed provider.
title: Medication Reconciliation

locator: Medication Administration §3 High-Alert Medications
quote:
High-Alert Medications
Medications with heightened risk of harm (anticoagulants, insulin, concentrated electrolytes, opioids,
chemotherapy) must have additional safeguards including independent double-checks, special labeling, and
restricted access.
title: High-Alert Medications

locator: Medication Administration §4 Controlled Substance Management
quote:
Controlled Substance Management
Controlled substances must be stored in double-locked secure areas, counted at each shift change, and all waste
must be witnessed and documented. Discrepancies must be reported and investigated immediately.
title: Controlled Substance Management

locator: Medication Administration §5 Adverse Drug Event Reporting
quote:
Adverse Drug Event Reporting
All adverse drug events, near-misses, and medication errors must be reported through the incident reporting
system and analyzed for root cause to prevent recurrence.
title: Adverse Drug Event Reporting

locator: Transfer and Discharge Procedures §1 Transfer Criteria & Authorization
quote:
Transfer Criteria & Authorization
Transfers must be medically appropriate. A physician must certify that the benefits of transfer outweigh the risks.
The patient must be stabilized to the extent possible within the facility's capabilities prior to transfer.
title: Transfer Criteria & Authorization

locator: Transfer and Discharge Procedures §2 Receiving Facility Acceptance
quote:
Receiving Facility Acceptance
The transferring hospital must confirm that the receiving facility has the capability and capacity to treat the patient
and has agreed to accept the patient prior to transfer initiation.
title: Receiving Facility Acceptance

locator: Transfer and Discharge Procedures §3 Transfer Documentation
quote:
Transfer Documentation
A copy of the medical record (or relevant portions) must accompany the patient. This includes: vital signs,
assessment findings, treatments provided, labs/imaging, and reason for transfer.
title: Transfer Documentation

locator: Transfer and Discharge Procedures §4 Patient Notification & Rights
quote:
Patient Notification & Rights
Patients must be informed of: the reason for transfer, the name of the receiving facility, their right to refuse transfer
(with documentation of risks of refusal), and their rights at the receiving facility.
title: Patient Notification & Rights

locator: Transfer and Discharge Procedures §5 Discharge Planning
quote:
Discharge Planning
Discharge planning must begin at admission. The plan must be patient-centered, involve the patient/family,
address post-acute care needs, include follow-up appointments, and provide education on medications and
warning signs.
title: Discharge Planning

locator: Restraint and Seclusion Policies §1 Least Restrictive Alternatives
quote:
Least Restrictive Alternatives
Before applying restraints or seclusion, staff must attempt and document less restrictive interventions. The
patient's behavior must represent a clear and present danger to self or others that cannot be managed by less
restrictive means.
title: Least Restrictive Alternatives

locator: Restraint and Seclusion Policies §2 Order Requirements
quote:
Order Requirements
Restraints require a physician or licensed independent practitioner order. Orders must specify: type of restraint,
clinical justification, and time limit (4 hours for adults, 2 hours for ages 9-17, 1 hour for under age 9). Telephone
orders must be confirmed in writing within 24 hours.
title: Order Requirements

locator: Restraint and Seclusion Policies §3 Monitoring Requirements
quote:
Monitoring Requirements
Patients in restraints must have continuous assessment. Monitoring includes: vital signs, circulation/sensation in
restrained extremities, skin integrity, nutrition/hydration, elimination, psychological status, and readiness for
restraint removal.
title: Monitoring Requirements

locator: Restraint and Seclusion Policies §4 Behavioral Health Restraints
quote:
Behavioral Health Restraints
Additional requirements apply for restraints/seclusion used for behavioral management: face-to-face evaluation
within 1 hour of initiation by a physician or trained RN/PA, and more frequent monitoring.
title: Behavioral Health Restraints

locator: Restraint and Seclusion Policies §5 Documentation & Reporting
quote:
Documentation & Reporting
All restraint use must be thoroughly documented. Deaths or serious injuries occurring while in restraints or within
24 hours of removal must be reported to CMS within 24 hours.
title: Documentation & Reporting

locator: Patient Privacy and HIPAA Compliance §1 Notice of Privacy Practices
quote:
Notice of Privacy Practices
Hospitals must provide patients with a Notice of Privacy Practices (NPP) at first contact, post the NPP prominently,
and make good-faith efforts to obtain written acknowledgment of receipt from patients.
title: Notice of Privacy Practices

locator: Patient Privacy and HIPAA Compliance §2 Minimum Necessary Standard
quote:
Minimum Necessary Standard
Staff may only access PHI that is necessary to perform their job functions. Role-based access controls must be
implemented and enforced. Accessing records of patients not under one's direct care (including celebrity or VIP
patients) is a violation.
title: Minimum Necessary Standard

locator: Patient Privacy and HIPAA Compliance §3 Patient Access Rights
quote:
Patient Access Rights
Patients have the right to: access and obtain copies of their health records, request amendments, receive an
accounting of disclosures, request restrictions on certain disclosures, and request confidential communications.
title: Patient Access Rights

locator: Patient Privacy and HIPAA Compliance §4 Breach Notification
quote:
Breach Notification
Any breach of unsecured PHI must be reported to affected individuals within 60 days of discovery, to HHS
annually (or immediately for breaches affecting 500+ individuals), and to media for large breaches affecting the
local community.
title: Breach Notification

locator: Patient Privacy and HIPAA Compliance §5 Technical Safeguards
quote:
Technical Safeguards
Electronic PHI (ePHI) must be protected through: access controls, audit logs, encryption, automatic logoff, integrity
controls, and transmission security. Mobile devices with ePHI must be encrypted and remotely wipeable.
title: Technical Safeguards

locator: Nursing Staff Supervision §1 Registered Nurse Requirement
quote:
Registered Nurse Requirement
A Registered Nurse (RN) must supervise and evaluate the nursing care for each patient. An RN must be on duty
24 hours a day, 7 days a week. Licensed Practical Nurses (LPNs) and nursing assistants must work under RN
supervision.
title: Registered Nurse Requirement

locator: Nursing Staff Supervision §2 Scope of Practice Compliance
quote:
Scope of Practice Compliance
Nursing staff must practice within their state-defined scope of practice. Supervisors are responsible for ensuring
delegated tasks are appropriate and performed by qualified individuals. Scope of practice violations must be
addressed immediately.
title: Scope of Practice Compliance

locator: Nursing Staff Supervision §3 Competency Validation
quote:
Competency Validation
All nursing staff must demonstrate competency for their assigned responsibilities before practicing independently.
Annual competency validation is required. Competency records must be maintained and accessible.
title: Competency Validation

locator: Nursing Staff Supervision §4 Supervision of Agency/Contract Staff
quote:
Supervision of Agency/Contract Staff
Agency and travel nurses must be oriented to hospital policies and patient population before patient care
assignment. They must be supervised by permanent staff and cannot hold charge nurse positions without hospital
administrator approval.
title: Supervision of Agency/Contract Staff

locator: Nursing Staff Supervision §5 Float Pool Management
quote:
Float Pool Management
Nurses floated to other units must be assessed for competency on that unit before assignment. Float nurses
should not be assigned patients requiring specialty skills they have not demonstrated competency in.
title: Float Pool Management

locator: Environment of Care - Hazardous Materials §1 Hazardous Materials Management
quote:
Hazardous Materials Management
A comprehensive hazardous materials inventory (HazMat) must be maintained. Safety Data Sheets (SDS) must
be readily accessible. Staff must receive training on hazardous materials they work with, including proper handling,
storage, and spill response.
title: Hazardous Materials Management

locator: Environment of Care - Hazardous Materials §2 Medical Waste Disposal
quote:
Medical Waste Disposal
Regulated medical waste (biohazardous waste, sharps, chemotherapy waste, pharmaceutical waste) must be
segregated, labeled, stored, transported, treated, and disposed of in compliance with federal, state, and local
regulations.
title: Medical Waste Disposal

locator: Environment of Care - Hazardous Materials §3 Utility Systems Management
quote:
Utility Systems Management
Critical utility systems (electrical, HVAC, medical gas, water) must be maintained, tested, and monitored. Backup
systems must be operational. Procedures for utility failures must be documented and staff must be trained.
title: Utility Systems Management

locator: Environment of Care - Hazardous Materials §4 Life Safety & Fire Prevention
quote:
Life Safety & Fire Prevention
Fire prevention programs must include: fire risk assessments, fire safety equipment maintenance, exit
accessibility, smoking policies, and regular fire drills. The Life Safety Code (NFPA 101) must be followed.
title: Life Safety & Fire Prevention

locator: Environment of Care - Hazardous Materials §5 Security Management
quote:
Security Management
A Security Risk Assessment must be performed regularly. Security measures must address: workplace violence
prevention, infant/child abduction prevention, management of violent or disruptive patients, and protection of staff.
title: Security Management

locator: Emergency Preparedness - Disaster Plan §1 Risk Assessment & Planning
quote:
Risk Assessment & Planning
An all-hazards risk assessment must be conducted to identify likely emergency events (natural disasters, mass
casualty incidents, utility failures, cyber attacks, pandemics). The Emergency Operations Plan (EOP) must
address each identified risk.
title: Risk Assessment & Planning

locator: Emergency Preparedness - Disaster Plan §2 Communications Plan
quote:
Communications Plan
An emergency communications plan must include: backup communications systems, procedures for notifying staff,
contact information for external agencies, patient tracking systems, and methods for communicating with
patients/families during emergencies.
title: Communications Plan

locator: Emergency Preparedness - Disaster Plan §3 Policies and Procedures
quote:
Policies and Procedures
The EOP must include procedures for: evacuation, sheltering in place, staff roles and responsibilities, supply chain
management during shortages, volunteer management, and continuity of essential services.
title: Policies and Procedures

locator: Emergency Preparedness - Disaster Plan §4 Training and Testing
quote:
Training and Testing
The program must be tested twice annually: at least one full-scale exercise and one additional exercise (which
may be tabletop). Exercises must involve community partners and external stakeholders when possible.
title: Training and Testing

locator: Emergency Preparedness - Disaster Plan §5 After-Action Review
quote:
After-Action Review
Following each drill or actual emergency, an after-action review must be conducted, documented, and used to
update the EOP. Lessons learned must be incorporated within 90 days of the exercise.
title: After-Action Review

locator: Patient Abuse - Harassment Policy §1 Definitions and Prohibited Conduct
quote:
Definitions and Prohibited Conduct
Policy must clearly define: physical abuse, verbal abuse, psychological abuse, sexual abuse, neglect, exploitation,
and harassment. All forms are prohibited. Patients must be informed of their right to be free from abuse as part of
the Patient Rights notice.
title: Definitions and Prohibited Conduct

locator: Patient Abuse - Harassment Policy §2 Reporting Obligations
quote:
Reporting Obligations
All staff, volunteers, and contractors have a mandatory duty to report suspected or witnessed abuse. Reports must
be made immediately through established channels. Mandatory reporting to state and local authorities must
comply with applicable law.
title: Reporting Obligations

locator: Patient Abuse - Harassment Policy §3 Investigation Protocol
quote:
Investigation Protocol
All allegations must be investigated promptly by individuals who are objective and independent of the accused.
Investigation findings must be documented. Accused staff must be removed from patient care pending
investigation outcome.
title: Investigation Protocol

locator: Patient Abuse - Harassment Policy §4 Victim Support
quote:
Victim Support
Victims of abuse must receive immediate protection, appropriate clinical care, emotional support, and access to
advocacy resources. Incidents must be handled with sensitivity and confidentiality.
title: Victim Support

locator: Patient Abuse - Harassment Policy §5 Corrective Action
quote:
Corrective Action
Substantiated abuse by staff must result in appropriate disciplinary action up to and including termination. State
licensing board notification and OIG exclusion database reporting must occur as required.
title: Corrective Action

locator: Staffing and Delivery of Care §1 Staffing Plan Development
quote:
Staffing Plan Development
A written staffing plan must be developed that considers: patient volume, patient acuity, unit layout, staff mix (RN,
LPN, CNA), available support services, and national staffing benchmarks. The plan must be approved by nursing
leadership.
title: Staffing Plan Development

locator: Staffing and Delivery of Care §2 Acuity-Based Staffing
quote:
Acuity-Based Staffing
Patient assignments must be based on acuity and complexity of care needs, not just census. A validated patient
classification/acuity system should be used. High-acuity patients require more experienced nurses with lower
patient-to-nurse ratios.
title: Acuity-Based Staffing

locator: Staffing and Delivery of Care §3 Charge Nurse Responsibilities
quote:
Charge Nurse Responsibilities
Charge nurses must monitor unit staffing throughout the shift and escalate staffing concerns to supervisors. They
must ensure equitable patient assignments and support staff in managing high-acuity situations.
title: Charge Nurse Responsibilities

locator: Staffing and Delivery of Care §4 Float and Agency Utilization
quote:
Float and Agency Utilization
Internal float pools should be utilized before external agency staff. Agency utilization should be minimized and
tracked. Overtime must be managed to prevent staff fatigue-related errors.
title: Float and Agency Utilization

locator: Staffing and Delivery of Care §5 Staffing Variance Documentation
quote:
Staffing Variance Documentation
When staffing falls below the approved plan, the variance must be documented including: the reason, the actual
staffing, corrective actions taken, and impact on patient care. Patterns of understaffing must be escalated to
administration.
title: Staffing Variance Documentation

locator: Credentialing and Supervision of Contract Staff §1 Initial Credentialing
quote:
Initial Credentialing
All practitioners must complete a rigorous initial credentialing process including: verification of education and
training, licensure verification with primary source, board certification, work history, professional references,
malpractice history review, and criminal background check.
title: Initial Credentialing

locator: Credentialing and Supervision of Contract Staff §2 Privileging Process
quote:
Privileging Process
Clinical privileges must be specific to each practitioner's demonstrated competencies and within the scope of the
hospital's services. Privileges must be based on education, training, experience, and demonstrated current
competence.
title: Privileging Process

locator: Credentialing and Supervision of Contract Staff §3 Ongoing Professional Practice Evaluation (OPPE)
quote:
Ongoing Professional Practice Evaluation (OPPE)
Ongoing monitoring of practitioner performance must occur at least every 12 months. OPPE data must include:
case volume, outcomes, quality metrics, and peer review findings. Results must inform privilege renewal
decisions.
title: Ongoing Professional Practice Evaluation (OPPE)

locator: Credentialing and Supervision of Contract Staff §4 Focused Professional Practice Evaluation (FPPE)
quote:
Focused Professional Practice Evaluation (FPPE)
Focused evaluation must be triggered by: initial privilege grant, new privileges, identified performance concerns, or
significant adverse events. FPPE criteria and monitoring methods must be defined in advance.
title: Focused Professional Practice Evaluation (FPPE)

locator: Credentialing and Supervision of Contract Staff §5 Contract Staff Requirements
quote:
Contract Staff Requirements
Contract and locum tenens practitioners must meet the same credentialing and privileging standards as employed
staff. Credentials may not be accepted from a staffing agency without independent primary source verification.
title: Contract Staff Requirements

locator: Quality Assurance - Performance Improvement (QAPI) §1 Program Design & Scope
quote:
Program Design & Scope
The QAPI program must address: patient safety, medical errors/near misses, utilization of services, patient
outcomes, patient and family experience, care transitions, and regulatory compliance. The scope must encompass
all departments, services, and settings of care.
title: Program Design & Scope

locator: Quality Assurance - Performance Improvement (QAPI) §2 Data Collection & Analysis
quote:
Data Collection & Analysis
Performance data must be systematically collected and analyzed using valid statistical methods. Measures must
include: process measures, outcome measures, and patient experience measures. Data must be compared to
national benchmarks.
title: Data Collection & Analysis

locator: Quality Assurance - Performance Improvement (QAPI) §3 Performance Improvement Projects
quote:
Performance Improvement Projects
Focused improvement projects must be conducted when data identifies significant performance gaps. Projects
must use a structured improvement methodology (PDSA, Lean, Six Sigma) and be data-driven throughout.
title: Performance Improvement Projects

locator: Quality Assurance - Performance Improvement (QAPI) §4 Adverse Events & Root Cause Analysis
quote:
Adverse Events & Root Cause Analysis
All serious adverse events, sentinel events, and never events must be analyzed through root cause analysis
(RCA). Action plans must address root causes, and effectiveness must be monitored. Near-misses should also be
analyzed for system improvement.
title: Adverse Events & Root Cause Analysis

locator: Quality Assurance - Performance Improvement (QAPI) §5 Governing Body Reporting
quote:
Governing Body Reporting
QAPI program results, including performance trends, improvement project outcomes, and adverse events, must be
reported to the Governing Body at least quarterly. The Governing Body must provide oversight and allocate
resources for improvement.
title: Governing Body Reporting

locator: Do Not Resuscitate DNR - POLST Orders §1 Advance Directive Inquiry
quote:
Advance Directive Inquiry
At the time of admission, every patient must be asked whether they have an advance directive. The presence or
absence of an advance directive must be documented in the medical record. Copies must be obtained and placed
in the chart.
title: Advance Directive Inquiry

locator: Do Not Resuscitate DNR - POLST Orders §2 DNR Order Requirements
quote:
DNR Order Requirements
DNR orders must be written by a physician or licensed independent practitioner. Verbal DNR orders must be
documented, signed, and co-signed. DNR status must be clearly communicated during handoffs and visible in the
medical record.
title: DNR Order Requirements

locator: Do Not Resuscitate DNR - POLST Orders §3 POLST/MOLST Implementation
quote:
POLST/MOLST Implementation
Portable Medical Orders (POLST/MOLST) must be honored upon patient presentation. Staff must be trained to
recognize and differentiate POLST from standard advance directives and understand the scope of each section.
title: POLST/MOLST Implementation

locator: Do Not Resuscitate DNR - POLST Orders §4 Patient/Family Communication
quote:
Patient/Family Communication
When patients lack capacity, surrogate decision-makers must be identified in priority order per state law.
Goals-of-care conversations should be documented including who was present, what was discussed, and the
decisions reached.
title: Patient/Family Communication

locator: Do Not Resuscitate DNR - POLST Orders §5 Code Status in Perioperative Settings
quote:
Code Status in Perioperative Settings
Facilities must have a specific policy addressing DNR orders in the surgical/anesthesia setting, including a
required conversation between surgeon, anesthesiologist, and patient/surrogate before any procedure regarding
suspension or continuation of DNR status.
title: Code Status in Perioperative Settings

locator: Surgical and Procedural Safety §1 Pre-Procedure Verification
quote:
Pre-Procedure Verification
A pre-procedure verification process must confirm the correct patient (two identifiers), correct procedure, correct
site/side, and availability of required documents, imaging, equipment, and implants before the patient leaves the
pre-operative area.
title: Pre-Procedure Verification

locator: Surgical and Procedural Safety §2 Site Marking
quote:
Site Marking
The operative or procedure site must be marked by the licensed practitioner who will perform the procedure.
Marking must be done with the patient awake and aware when possible. The mark must be visible after prepping
and draping.
title: Site Marking

locator: Surgical and Procedural Safety §3 Time-Out Procedure
quote:
Time-Out Procedure
Immediately before starting any invasive procedure, the entire team must pause for a time-out. All team members
must actively participate and confirm: patient identity, procedure, site/side, patient position, and availability of
critical equipment.
title: Time-Out Procedure

locator: Surgical and Procedural Safety §4 Surgical Count Policy
quote:
Surgical Count Policy
Sponge, sharps, and instrument counts must be performed and documented according to AORN standards at the
beginning of the procedure, before closure of any body cavity, at wound closure, and at shift change.
title: Surgical Count Policy

locator: Surgical and Procedural Safety §5 Specimen Management
quote:
Specimen Management
Surgical specimens must be labeled immediately in the sterile field, with the patient's name, MRN, specimen
source, and laterality. Chain of custody documentation must accompany specimens to pathology.
title: Specimen Management

locator: Blood Product Transfusion Reaction DETAILED §1 STOP the Transfusion Immediately
quote:
STOP the Transfusion Immediately
Clamp the blood tubing at the IV site. Do NOT remove the IV access. Do NOT discard the blood product or
tubing — both are required for the reaction workup.
title: STOP the Transfusion Immediately

locator: Blood Product Transfusion Reaction DETAILED §2 Maintain IV Access with Normal Saline
quote:
Maintain IV Access with Normal Saline
Keep the IV patent by infusing 0.9% Normal Saline (NS) through NEW IV tubing connected directly to the IV
catheter. Do NOT flush blood product into the patient using existing tubing.
title: Maintain IV Access with Normal Saline

locator: Blood Product Transfusion Reaction DETAILED §3 Perform Rapid Patient Assessment
quote:
Perform Rapid Patient Assessment
Obtain vital signs (temperature, BP, HR, RR, SpO■). Perform focused assessment: skin (rash, flushing,
hives), respiratory (wheezing, distress), renal (urine color), neurological (LOC, complaint of pain). Assign
severity: mild / moderate / severe.
title: Perform Rapid Patient Assessment

locator: Blood Product Transfusion Reaction DETAILED §4 Notify Physician and Blood Bank Immediately
quote:
Notify Physician and Blood Bank Immediately
Contact the attending physician or rapid response team (for moderate/severe reactions). Simultaneously
notify the Blood Bank of the suspected reaction. Provide: unit number, patient name/MRN, time transfusion
started, time reaction noted, current vital signs, and symptoms.
title: Notify Physician and Blood Bank Immediately

locator: Blood Product Transfusion Reaction DETAILED §5 Collect Post-Reaction Specimens
quote:
Collect Post-Reaction Specimens
Draw the following BEFORE any additional IV fluids are given when possible:  1 pink-top (EDTA) tube —
repeat type & crossmatch, DAT  1 red-top (SST) tube — plasma for hemolysis evaluation (BMP, LDH,
haptoglobin, bilirubin)  Urine specimen — free hemoglobin (hemoglobinuria)  Blood cultures × 2 sets if septic
reaction is suspected Label specimens with TWO patient identifiers and mark clearly as 'TRANSFUSION
title: Collect Post-Reaction Specimens

locator: Blood Product Transfusion Reaction DETAILED §6 Return Blood Product and Tubing to Blood Bank
quote:
Return Blood Product and Tubing to Blood Bank
Return the implicated blood bag (with all attached tubing, intact and clamped), the transfusion record, and any
IV solutions co-infused. The blood bank will inspect the unit and perform a clerical check.
title: Return Blood Product and Tubing to Blood Bank

locator: Blood Product Transfusion Reaction DETAILED §7 Administer Treatment as Ordered
quote:
Administer Treatment as Ordered
Treatment is reaction-specific and physician-directed:  Allergic/urticarial: Diphenhydramine 25–50 mg IV/IM
per order  Anaphylaxis: Epinephrine 0.3–0.5 mg IM (1:1,000) immediately; call Code/RRT  AHTR/Hemolytic:
IV fluids to maintain UO ≥1 mL/kg/hr; furosemide per order; monitor renal function  TACO: Furosemide 20–40
mg IV; upright positioning; supplemental O■  Febrile (FNHTR confirmed): Acetaminophen 650 mg PO/PR
per order  Septic: Blood cultures × 2; broad-spectrum antibiotics per order; notify pharmacy and ID
title: Administer Treatment as Ordered

locator: Blood Product Transfusion Reaction DETAILED §8 Document in the Medical Record
quote:
Document in the Medical Record
Complete nursing documentation must include: time transfusion began, time reaction noted, vital signs trend
(pre/during/post), symptoms described by the patient and observed, all interventions performed with times,
name and time of physician notification, patient response to treatment, and disposition of blood product.
title: Document in the Medical Record

locator: Blood Product Transfusion Reaction DETAILED §9 Complete Transfusion Reaction Report
quote:
Complete Transfusion Reaction Report
Complete the facility transfusion reaction report form within 1 hour of reaction identification. Submit to the
Blood Bank AND enter a Patient Safety Event (incident) report in the occurrence reporting system. Do not
delay reporting pending lab results.
title: Complete Transfusion Reaction Report

locator: Blood Product Transfusion Reaction DETAILED §10 Monitor Patient Post-Reaction
quote:
Monitor Patient Post-Reaction
Vital signs and assessment every 15 minutes × 4, then every 30 minutes × 2, then per unit protocol. Monitor
urine output. If transfusion is to be resumed (mild allergic only, after physician order and symptom resolution),
restart at ≤1 mL/kg/hr with bedside nurse present for first 15 minutes.
title: Monitor Patient Post-Reaction

locator: Blood and Blood Product Administration §1 Pre-Transfusion Requirements
quote:
Pre-Transfusion Requirements
Informed consent for blood transfusion must be obtained and documented before non-emergent transfusions. A
current type and screen (within 3 days for non-pregnant patients, per facility policy) must be on file. Two-person
verification of the blood product and patient identification is mandatory.
title: Pre-Transfusion Requirements

locator: Blood and Blood Product Administration §2 Patient Identification at Bedside
quote:
Patient Identification at Bedside
Before hanging any blood product, two licensed staff members must independently verify: patient name, date of
birth, MRN, blood type, unit number, expiration date, and any special processing requirements at the bedside
using the patient's armband.
title: Patient Identification at Bedside

locator: Blood and Blood Product Administration §3 Transfusion Administration
quote:
Transfusion Administration
Blood products must be administered through an appropriate filter within 4 hours of issue from the blood bank.
Vital signs must be taken before the transfusion, 15 minutes after initiation, and upon completion. The first 15
minutes must be observed by a nurse.
title: Transfusion Administration

locator: Blood and Blood Product Administration §4 Transfusion Reaction Management
quote:
Transfusion Reaction Management
If a transfusion reaction is suspected (fever, chills, urticaria, back/flank pain, hemoglobinuria, hypotension), the
transfusion must be stopped immediately, IV line kept open with NS, physician notified, and the blood bank notified
to begin reaction workup.
title: Transfusion Reaction Management

locator: Blood and Blood Product Administration §5 Blood Bank Inventory Management
quote:
Blood Bank Inventory Management
Policies must address emergency release procedures, massive transfusion protocols (MTP), autologous blood
handling, and management of patients who refuse blood products for religious reasons.
title: Blood Bank Inventory Management

locator: Fall Prevention Program §1 Fall Risk Assessment
quote:
Fall Risk Assessment
A validated fall risk assessment tool (Morse Fall Scale, STRATIFY, or equivalent) must be completed on
admission, after any fall, after a change in condition, and with each shift assessment. Risk level must be
documented and communicated during handoffs.
title: Fall Risk Assessment

locator: Fall Prevention Program §2 Universal Fall Precautions
quote:
Universal Fall Precautions
All patients, regardless of risk score, must receive: bed in lowest position, call light within reach, non-slip footwear,
clear path to bathroom, and orientation to environment. Environmental safety rounds must be conducted each
shift.
title: Universal Fall Precautions

locator: Fall Prevention Program §3 High-Risk Interventions
quote:
High-Risk Interventions
High fall-risk patients require additional interventions including: yellow fall-risk armband, bed/chair alarm, hourly
rounding, toileting schedule, fall-risk signage, and removal of unnecessary equipment from room. Consider bed
exit sensor alarms for highest-risk patients.
title: High-Risk Interventions

locator: Fall Prevention Program §4 Post-Fall Management
quote:
Post-Fall Management
Following any fall: ensure patient safety and assess for injury, notify physician, complete incident report, perform
post-fall huddle within 24 hours with bedside team, and conduct root cause review. CT head/imaging as ordered
for head strikes.
title: Post-Fall Management

locator: Fall Prevention Program §5 Patient and Family Education
quote:
Patient and Family Education
Patients and families must be educated on fall risk, the importance of calling for assistance, how to use the call
light, and safe mobility techniques. Education must be documented and reinforced throughout hospitalization.
title: Patient and Family Education

locator: Pressure Injury Prevention and Treatment §1 Skin Assessment on Admission
quote:
Skin Assessment on Admission
A head-to-toe skin assessment must be completed and documented within 8 hours of inpatient admission (within 2
hours for high-risk populations). All existing wounds, pressure injuries, and areas of concern must be
photographed and documented with stage, location, and measurements.
title: Skin Assessment on Admission

locator: Pressure Injury Prevention and Treatment §2 Risk Assessment
quote:
Risk Assessment
A validated risk assessment tool (Braden Scale, Norton Scale) must be completed on admission, every 24 hours
for hospitalized patients, and with any change in condition. Patients with Braden score ≤18 require a documented
prevention care plan.
title: Risk Assessment

locator: Pressure Injury Prevention and Treatment §3 Prevention Interventions
quote:
Prevention Interventions
Prevention care plans must be individualized based on risk factors and include: repositioning schedule (minimum
every 2 hours), pressure-redistribution mattress/surfaces for at-risk patients, moisture management, nutritional
support, and heel offloading.
title: Prevention Interventions

locator: Pressure Injury Prevention and Treatment §4 Wound Assessment and Documentation
quote:
Wound Assessment and Documentation
All pressure injuries must be assessed and documented with each dressing change using the PUSH tool or
equivalent: stage, dimensions, wound bed characteristics, exudate, periwound condition, and pain. Photography at
admission and with significant changes is required.
title: Wound Assessment and Documentation

locator: Pressure Injury Prevention and Treatment §5 Wound Care Orders and Treatment
quote:
Wound Care Orders and Treatment
Wound care orders must be specific and include: cleansing agent, dressing type, frequency of change, and
offloading requirements. Complex wounds should have wound care specialist consultation. Treatment must be
consistent with evidence-based guidelines.
title: Wound Care Orders and Treatment

locator: Patient Identification Policy §1 Acceptable Identifiers
quote:
Acceptable Identifiers
Two patient-specific identifiers must be used before any care delivery. Acceptable identifiers include: patient
name, date of birth, and medical record number. Room number and bed number are NOT acceptable identifiers.
Staff must ask the patient to state their name, not confirm a stated name.
title: Acceptable Identifiers

locator: Patient Identification Policy §2 Armband Requirements
quote:
Armband Requirements
All inpatients must wear a hospital-issued identification armband at all times. Armbands must contain at minimum:
full name, date of birth, and MRN. Allergy armbands (red) and fall-risk armbands (yellow) must be applied per
policy.
title: Armband Requirements

locator: Patient Identification Policy §3 Specimen Labeling
quote:
Specimen Labeling
All specimens must be labeled at the bedside immediately after collection with two patient identifiers, date/time of
collection, and collector's name. Pre-labeled tubes must NOT be used. Unlabeled specimens must be rejected by
the laboratory.
title: Specimen Labeling

locator: Patient Identification Policy §4 Medication Verification
quote:
Medication Verification
Two patient identifiers must be verified before administering any medication. Barcode Medication Administration
(BCMA) systems support but do not replace the verification requirement. Nurses must scan both the patient
armband and the medication before administration.
title: Medication Verification

locator: Patient Identification Policy §5 Newborn and Pediatric Identification
quote:
Newborn and Pediatric Identification
Newborns must receive two identification bands placed in the delivery room. Mother-baby banding must be verified
before any infant is removed from the mother. Pediatric patients who cannot verbally confirm identity must have a
parent/guardian confirm.
title: Newborn and Pediatric Identification

locator: Sepsis Recognition and Management §1 Sepsis Screening
quote:
Sepsis Screening
All clinical staff must be trained to recognize signs and symptoms of sepsis. Sepsis screening tools must be
applied at triage, admission, and with any change in clinical condition. Electronic health record-based sepsis alerts
support but do not replace clinical assessment.
title: Sepsis Screening

locator: Sepsis Recognition and Management §2 3-Hour Bundle Compliance (Severe Sepsis)
quote:
3-Hour Bundle Compliance (Severe Sepsis)
Within 3 hours of severe sepsis recognition: obtain blood cultures (before antibiotics), measure lactate level,
administer broad-spectrum antibiotics, and provide 30 mL/kg crystalloid bolus for hypotension or lactate ≥4
mmol/L.
title: 3-Hour Bundle Compliance (Severe Sepsis)

locator: Sepsis Recognition and Management §3 6-Hour Bundle Compliance (Septic Shock)
quote:
6-Hour Bundle Compliance (Septic Shock)
Within 6 hours of septic shock recognition: apply vasopressors for MAP <65 mmHg, re-measure lactate if initial
lactate ≥2 mmol/L, and reassess volume status and tissue perfusion with documented reassessment.
title: 6-Hour Bundle Compliance (Septic Shock)

locator: Sepsis Recognition and Management §4 Escalation and Notification
quote:
Escalation and Notification
Defined escalation protocols must ensure timely physician notification for sepsis recognition. Rapid Response
Team (RRT) activation criteria must include sepsis indicators. Critical care consultation should be triggered for
septic shock.
title: Escalation and Notification

locator: Sepsis Recognition and Management §5 Antibiotic Stewardship Integration
quote:
Antibiotic Stewardship Integration
Antibiotic selection for sepsis must balance broad empiric coverage with stewardship principles. Blood cultures
must be obtained before antibiotics. De-escalation to targeted therapy must occur within 24-72 hours based on
culture results.
title: Antibiotic Stewardship Integration

locator: Stroke Care Protocol §1 Code Stroke Activation
quote:
Code Stroke Activation
A single activation number or system must initiate a coordinated Code Stroke response. The response team must
include: emergency physician, neurologist (or teleneurology), CT technician, pharmacist, and nursing. Target
door-to-CT time is under 25 minutes.
title: Code Stroke Activation

locator: Stroke Care Protocol §2 tPA/Thrombolytic Administration
quote:
tPA/Thrombolytic Administration
Eligible ischemic stroke patients must receive IV alteplase within 60 minutes of arrival (door-to-needle time). Strict
inclusion/exclusion criteria must be followed. A checklist-based workflow reduces errors. Endovascular treatment
(thrombectomy) must be considered for large vessel occlusion.
title: tPA/Thrombolytic Administration

locator: Stroke Care Protocol §3 Stroke Unit Care
quote:
Stroke Unit Care
Admitted stroke patients must be cared for in a dedicated stroke unit or by a stroke-trained team with access to:
continuous cardiac monitoring, dysphagia screening before oral intake, early PT/OT/speech therapy, and VTE
prophylaxis.
title: Stroke Unit Care

locator: Stroke Care Protocol §4 Secondary Prevention
quote:
Secondary Prevention
Before discharge, ischemic stroke patients must receive: antiplatelet therapy (or anticoagulation for AF-related
stroke), statin therapy, antihypertensive therapy, and smoking cessation counseling. Atrial fibrillation screening
must be performed.
title: Secondary Prevention

locator: Stroke Care Protocol §5 Stroke Education and Rehabilitation
quote:
Stroke Education and Rehabilitation
Patients and families must receive education on stroke recognition (FAST), risk factor modification, medication
adherence, and warning signs of recurrent stroke. Rehabilitation needs must be assessed and appropriate
post-acute care arranged.
title: Stroke Education and Rehabilitation

locator: Moderate and Deep Sedation Policy §1 Pre-Sedation Assessment
quote:
Pre-Sedation Assessment
A qualified practitioner must perform and document a pre-sedation assessment including: NPO status, relevant
medical history, medication/allergy review, airway assessment (Mallampati score), ASA physical status
classification, and consent for sedation.
title: Pre-Sedation Assessment

locator: Moderate and Deep Sedation Policy §2 Qualified Personnel
quote:
Qualified Personnel
Moderate sedation must be administered or supervised by a practitioner with documented competency in sedation
and airway management. A separate individual, other than the one performing the procedure, must monitor the
patient throughout.
title: Qualified Personnel

locator: Moderate and Deep Sedation Policy §3 Intraoperative Monitoring
quote:
Intraoperative Monitoring
Continuous monitoring must include: pulse oximetry, capnography (end-tidal CO2), cardiac rhythm, blood pressure
(minimum every 5 minutes), and level of consciousness using a validated scale (Ramsay, MOAA/S). Findings
must be documented on a sedation record.
title: Intraoperative Monitoring

locator: Moderate and Deep Sedation Policy §4 Rescue Capabilities
quote:
Rescue Capabilities
All sedation locations must have immediately available: supplemental oxygen, suction, bag-valve-mask,
resuscitation equipment, and reversal agents (flumazenil for benzodiazepines, naloxone for opioids). Personnel
must be trained in rescue ventilation and CPR.
title: Rescue Capabilities

locator: Moderate and Deep Sedation Policy §5 Post-Sedation Recovery
quote:
Post-Sedation Recovery
Patients must recover in a monitored setting until meeting defined discharge criteria (modified Aldrete score ≥9 or
equivalent). Discharge criteria, monitoring intervals during recovery, and discharge instructions must be
documented.
title: Post-Sedation Recovery

locator: Discharge Planning and Care Transitions §1 Early Discharge Planning Initiation
quote:
Early Discharge Planning Initiation
Discharge planning must begin within 24 hours of admission for all patients. A Registered Nurse or social worker
must conduct a discharge needs assessment including: living situation, support systems, functional status, home
safety, and financial resources.
title: Early Discharge Planning Initiation

locator: Discharge Planning and Care Transitions §2 Multidisciplinary Collaboration
quote:
Multidisciplinary Collaboration
The discharge planning process must involve all relevant disciplines: nursing, social work, case management,
physical/occupational therapy, pharmacy, and the attending physician. Multidisciplinary rounds should include
discharge planning as a standing agenda item.
title: Multidisciplinary Collaboration

locator: Discharge Planning and Care Transitions §3 Patient and Family Involvement
quote:
Patient and Family Involvement
The patient and/or designated representative must be involved in all discharge planning decisions. The planned
discharge destination must be discussed with the patient, and the patient's preferences must be considered.
Patients have the right to request a Quality Improvement Organization (QIO) review before discharge.
title: Patient and Family Involvement

locator: Discharge Planning and Care Transitions §4 Transition of Care Documentation
quote:
Transition of Care Documentation
The discharge summary must be completed and transmitted to the receiving provider within 24 hours of discharge
(or within 48 hours for complex patients). It must include: diagnosis, hospital course, medications, follow-up
appointments, and pending test results.
title: Transition of Care Documentation

locator: Discharge Planning and Care Transitions §5 Readmission Risk Reduction
quote:
Readmission Risk Reduction
High-risk patients (LACE score or equivalent) must receive enhanced transition services including: post-discharge
telephone follow-up within 48-72 hours, medication reconciliation at discharge, confirmed follow-up appointment,
and patient education on red-flag symptoms.
title: Readmission Risk Reduction

locator: Rapid Response Team RRT Policy §1 Activation Criteria
quote:
Activation Criteria
Any staff member, patient, or family member may activate the RRT without fear of reprisal. Clear activation criteria
must be posted and communicated, including: acute change in heart rate, respiratory rate, blood pressure, oxygen
saturation, mental status, or concern that the patient 'just doesn't look right.'
title: Activation Criteria

locator: Rapid Response Team RRT Policy §2 RRT Composition and Response Time
quote:
RRT Composition and Response Time
The RRT must include a minimum of: a critical care nurse or advanced practice provider and a respiratory
therapist. A physician must be available by phone or in person. The team must respond to the bedside within 5
minutes of activation.
title: RRT Composition and Response Time

locator: Rapid Response Team RRT Policy §3 RRT Assessment and Intervention
quote:
RRT Assessment and Intervention
The RRT must conduct a rapid systematic assessment using a standardized framework (SBAR, I-SBAR-R).
Interventions may include: airway management, IV access, fluid resuscitation, medication administration, and
arrangement of ICU transfer if needed.
title: RRT Assessment and Intervention

locator: Rapid Response Team RRT Policy §4 Documentation Requirements
quote:
Documentation Requirements
All RRT activations must be documented including: time of activation, team members present, clinical findings,
interventions performed, and patient disposition. A standardized RRT documentation tool must be used.
title: Documentation Requirements

locator: Rapid Response Team RRT Policy §5 Afferent and Efferent Limb Monitoring
quote:
Afferent and Efferent Limb Monitoring
RRT programs must monitor both the afferent limb (early warning system performance, including the number of
hours between deterioration and RRT activation) and the efferent limb (RRT response effectiveness and
outcomes). Data must drive program improvement.
title: Afferent and Efferent Limb Monitoring

locator: Pain Assessment and Management §1 Pain Assessment
quote:
Pain Assessment
Pain must be assessed using a validated, patient-appropriate tool (NRS 0-10 for cognitively intact adults, FLACC
or Wong-Baker for children, CPOT for non-verbal patients). Pain assessment must be performed on admission,
with every vital sign set, before and after pain interventions, and at discharge.
title: Pain Assessment

locator: Pain Assessment and Management §2 Multimodal Pain Management
quote:
Multimodal Pain Management
Pain management plans must consider multimodal approaches including: non-pharmacological interventions
(positioning, ice/heat, distraction), non-opioid medications (acetaminophen, NSAIDs, gabapentinoids),
regional/neuraxial techniques, and opioids reserved for when other methods are insufficient.
title: Multimodal Pain Management

locator: Pain Assessment and Management §3 Opioid Prescribing Safety
quote:
Opioid Prescribing Safety
Opioid orders must include: specific drug, dose, route, frequency, and indication. PRN opioid frequency must be
clinically appropriate. Concurrent CNS depressants (benzodiazepines, muscle relaxants) must be prescribed with
caution and documented rationale.
title: Opioid Prescribing Safety

locator: Pain Assessment and Management §4 High-Risk Patient Monitoring
quote:
High-Risk Patient Monitoring
Patients receiving opioids must be monitored for respiratory depression, sedation, and oxygen saturation.
High-risk patients (elderly, opioid-naive, obese, sleep apnea) require enhanced monitoring. Naloxone must be
available at the bedside for high-risk patients.
title: High-Risk Patient Monitoring

locator: Pain Assessment and Management §5 Opioid Use Disorder Considerations
quote:
Opioid Use Disorder Considerations
Patients with known or suspected opioid use disorder must receive concurrent addiction medicine consultation or
referral. Medication-assisted treatment (MAT) should be continued or initiated during hospitalization. PDMP
(Prescription Drug Monitoring Program) must be checked before prescribing opioids.
title: Opioid Use Disorder Considerations

locator: Pain Assessment and Reassessment DETAILED §1 O — Onset
quote:
O — Onset
When did the pain begin? Was the onset sudden or gradual? Was there a precipitating event?
title: O — Onset

locator: Pain Assessment and Reassessment DETAILED §2 P — Provocation / Palliation
quote:
P — Provocation / Palliation
What makes the pain better? What makes it worse? Does movement, position, heat, or cold affect it?
title: P — Provocation / Palliation

locator: Pain Assessment and Reassessment DETAILED §3 Q — Quality
quote:
Q — Quality
How would you describe the pain? (Aching, burning, stabbing, throbbing, pressure, shooting, cramping)
title: Q — Quality

locator: Pain Assessment and Reassessment DETAILED §4 R — Radiation / Region
quote:
R — Radiation / Region
Where is the pain located? Does it radiate anywhere? Point to the location with one finger.
title: R — Radiation / Region

locator: Pain Assessment and Reassessment DETAILED §5 S — Severity
quote:
S — Severity
Rate your pain on a scale of 0–10 (or appropriate validated tool). What is your acceptable/goal pain level?
title: S — Severity

locator: Pain Assessment and Reassessment DETAILED §6 T — Timing / Temporal Pattern
quote:
T — Timing / Temporal Pattern
Is the pain constant or intermittent? Is it getting better, worse, or staying the same? Duration of episodes?
title: T — Timing / Temporal Pattern

locator: Pain Assessment and Reassessment DETAILED §7 A — Associated Symptoms
quote:
A — Associated Symptoms
Are there associated symptoms? Nausea, shortness of breath, diaphoresis, numbness/tingling, weakness?
title: A — Associated Symptoms

locator: Pain Assessment and Reassessment DETAILED §8 A — Actions / Prior Treatment
quote:
A — Actions / Prior Treatment
What medications or interventions have been tried? What was the effect? Any allergies or adverse reactions?
title: A — Actions / Prior Treatment

locator: Pain Assessment and Reassessment DETAILED §1 Establish Discharge Pain Goal
quote:
Establish Discharge Pain Goal
Discuss with patient their acceptable pain level at home. Document goal and mutual agreement.
title: Establish Discharge Pain Goal

locator: Pain Assessment and Reassessment DETAILED §2 Reconcile Discharge Pain Medications
quote:
Reconcile Discharge Pain Medications
Ensure all pain medications are reconciled. Provide patient-friendly medication list with dose, frequency, and
purpose of each drug.
title: Reconcile Discharge Pain Medications

locator: Pain Assessment and Reassessment DETAILED §3 Opioid Discharge Counseling
quote:
Opioid Discharge Counseling
Counsel on: safe storage (locked), avoiding alcohol and CNS depressants, driving restrictions, constipation
prevention, naloxone co-prescription for high-risk patients, and safe disposal.
title: Opioid Discharge Counseling

locator: Pain Assessment and Reassessment DETAILED §4 Non-Opioid Strategy at Home
quote:
Non-Opioid Strategy at Home
Provide written plan for non-pharmacological strategies and scheduled non-opioid medications to reduce
opioid reliance post-discharge.
title: Non-Opioid Strategy at Home

locator: Pain Assessment and Reassessment DETAILED §5 Follow-Up Appointment Confirmation
quote:
Follow-Up Appointment Confirmation
Confirm follow-up appointment is scheduled. Provide contact number for pain questions. Instruct on warning
signs requiring emergency evaluation.
title: Follow-Up Appointment Confirmation

locator: Pain Assessment and Reassessment DETAILED §6 Patient Teach-Back
quote:
Patient Teach-Back
Verify patient/caregiver understanding using teach-back method. Document patient verbalized understanding
of pain management plan.
For internal clinical use only. Review annually and upon regulatory updates. This policy does not
replace clinical judgment.
 Policy 27 of 30 | Detailed Procedure
title: Patient Teach-Back

locator: Suicide Risk Screening and Prevention §1 Universal Screening
quote:
Universal Screening
All patients presenting to the emergency department and all inpatients admitted to behavioral health units must be
screened for suicide risk using a validated tool (Columbia Suicide Severity Rating Scale [C-SSRS] or ASQ).
Medical/surgical inpatients should be screened if risk factors are identified.
title: Universal Screening

locator: Suicide Risk Screening and Prevention §2 Risk Stratification and Interventions
quote:
Risk Stratification and Interventions
Screening results must be used to stratify risk (low, moderate, high) and determine appropriate interventions.
High-risk patients require: 1:1 continuous observation, removal of potentially harmful items, psychiatric
consultation, and immediate safety planning.
title: Risk Stratification and Interventions

locator: Suicide Risk Screening and Prevention §3 Environmental Safety / Ligature Risk
quote:
Environmental Safety / Ligature Risk
Patient care areas where patients at risk are treated must be assessed for and mitigated against ligature risks
(points where a cord, rope, or other material can be looped to create a hanging risk). Mitigation measures must be
documented and regularly evaluated.
title: Environmental Safety / Ligature Risk

locator: Suicide Risk Screening and Prevention §4 Safety Planning
quote:
Safety Planning
Individualized safety plans must be developed collaboratively with the patient, documented in the medical record,
and updated as clinical status changes. Safety plans must address: warning signs, coping strategies, reasons for
living, support contacts, and means restriction.
title: Safety Planning

locator: Suicide Risk Screening and Prevention §5 Transition Care and Means Restriction Counseling
quote:
Transition Care and Means Restriction Counseling
At discharge, patients identified as at risk must receive: crisis resources (988 Lifeline), follow-up appointment
within 7 days (Joint Commission standard), and means restriction counseling addressing access to lethal means
(firearms, medications).
title: Transition Care and Means Restriction Counseling

locator: Antibiotic Stewardship Program §1 Program Leadership and Accountability
quote:
Program Leadership and Accountability
The ASP must have a physician leader (infectious disease physician preferred) and a pharmacist leader with
stewardship training. Leadership must have the support and accountability of hospital administration. The program
must report to the infection control committee and QAPI.
title: Program Leadership and Accountability

locator: Antibiotic Stewardship Program §2 Core Stewardship Interventions
quote:
Core Stewardship Interventions
The ASP must implement evidence-based interventions including: prospective audit and feedback (review of
antimicrobial orders with prescriber feedback), prior authorization for high-risk/broad-spectrum agents, and dose
optimization based on renal function and PK/PD principles.
title: Core Stewardship Interventions

locator: Antibiotic Stewardship Program §3 Antibiogram and Formulary Management
quote:
Antibiogram and Formulary Management
An annual facility-specific antibiogram must be developed and disseminated to prescribers. Empiric antibiotic
selection should be guided by local resistance patterns. The formulary must limit availability of agents not aligned
with stewardship goals.
title: Antibiogram and Formulary Management

locator: Antibiotic Stewardship Program §4 Antibiotic Time-Outs
quote:
Antibiotic Time-Outs
A mandatory 48-72 hour antibiotic review (time-out) must be implemented for all patients receiving antibiotics. The
review should assess: cultures and sensitivities available, opportunity to de-escalate, appropriateness of continued
therapy, and transition to oral therapy.
title: Antibiotic Time-Outs

locator: Antibiotic Stewardship Program §5 Monitoring and Reporting
quote:
Monitoring and Reporting
Process and outcome metrics must be monitored including: antibiotic days of therapy per 1,000 patient days, C.
difficile rates, resistance rates for key organisms, and antibiotic expenditure. Data must be reported to prescribers
and quality leadership.
title: Monitoring and Reporting

locator: Workplace Violence Prevention §1 Workplace Violence Risk Assessment
quote:
Workplace Violence Risk Assessment
A systematic risk assessment of all hospital areas must be conducted to identify environmental, administrative,
and behavioral risk factors for violence. High-risk areas (ED, psychiatric units, waiting areas) require enhanced
preventive measures. Risk assessments must be updated annually and after incidents.
title: Workplace Violence Risk Assessment

locator: Workplace Violence Prevention §2 Prevention Strategies
quote:
Prevention Strategies
Prevention measures must include: visitor management and access control, duress alarm systems in high-risk
areas, metal detection in appropriate settings, patient behavioral risk flagging systems, adequate staffing levels
(inadequate staffing increases violence risk), and environmental design modifications.
title: Prevention Strategies

locator: Workplace Violence Prevention §3 De-escalation Training
quote:
De-escalation Training
All clinical staff must receive training in verbal de-escalation techniques before patient care assignment and
annually thereafter. Training must include: recognition of escalating behavior, communication strategies, safe
positioning, and when and how to request assistance.
title: De-escalation Training

locator: Workplace Violence Prevention §4 Incident Reporting and Response
quote:
Incident Reporting and Response
All workplace violence incidents must be reported without fear of retaliation. A standardized reporting process
must be in place. After any violent incident: ensure staff safety, provide medical care, initiate the incident reporting
process, preserve evidence, and notify appropriate parties including security and administration.
title: Incident Reporting and Response

locator: Workplace Violence Prevention §5 Post-Incident Support
quote:
Post-Incident Support
Staff involved in violent incidents must have access to: employee assistance program (EAP), peer support,
management debriefing, and time off if needed. Critical incident stress debriefing should be offered after serious
incidents. Return-to-work support must be provided.
title: Post-Incident Support

locator: Central Line Dressing Change DETAILED §1 Verify Order and Assess Need
quote:
Verify Order and Assess Need
Confirm a physician order for central line dressing change (or that the change is per standing protocol).
Assess dressing: is it due by schedule, or is it soiled, loose, lifting, bloody, or non-occlusive? Any of these
conditions require immediate dressing change regardless of schedule.
title: Verify Order and Assess Need

locator: Central Line Dressing Change DETAILED §2 Perform Hand Hygiene
quote:
Perform Hand Hygiene
Perform hand hygiene with ABHR or soap and water per WHO Five Moments protocol. This is Moment 2
(before an aseptic procedure). Do NOT skip this step even if you will be wearing gloves.
title: Perform Hand Hygiene

locator: Central Line Dressing Change DETAILED §3 Gather Supplies and Prepare Environment
quote:
Gather Supplies and Prepare Environment
Gather all required supplies before entering the room. Raise the bed to working height. Position patient for
access to catheter insertion site. Ensure adequate lighting. Close room door or curtain. Turn patient's face
away from the insertion site.
title: Gather Supplies and Prepare Environment

locator: Central Line Dressing Change DETAILED §4 Apply Masks
quote:
Apply Masks
Apply a surgical mask over your nose and mouth. Instruct the patient to apply a surgical mask (or turn their
face away and avoid talking, coughing, or sneezing toward the insertion site during the procedure). This is a
required CLABSI prevention measure.
title: Apply Masks

locator: Central Line Dressing Change DETAILED §5 Open Sterile Supplies Using Aseptic Technique
quote:
Open Sterile Supplies Using Aseptic Technique
Open the dressing change kit and all supplies onto a clean, dry surface using aseptic non-touch technique. Do
NOT contaminate the inner sterile field. Open CHG applicator, Biopatch, and TSM dressing packaging and
place on the sterile field without touching sterile surfaces with ungloved hands.
title: Open Sterile Supplies Using Aseptic Technique

locator: Central Line Dressing Change DETAILED §6 Don Clean Gloves and Remove Old Dressing
quote:
Don Clean Gloves and Remove Old Dressing
Apply clean (non-sterile) gloves. Remove the old dressing by peeling edges toward the insertion site (to avoid
dislodging the catheter). Stabilize the catheter hub with your non-dominant hand while removing dressing.
Note: dressing removal direction matters — always toward the catheter, never away. Assess old dressing for:
drainage, odor, blood, condition of Biopatch.
title: Don Clean Gloves and Remove Old Dressing

locator: Central Line Dressing Change DETAILED §7 Remove Clean Gloves and Perform Hand Hygiene
quote:
Remove Clean Gloves and Perform Hand Hygiene
Remove and discard clean gloves. Perform hand hygiene with ABHR immediately before donning sterile
gloves. This is a critical step that is frequently skipped — it is mandatory.
title: Remove Clean Gloves and Perform Hand Hygiene

locator: Central Line Dressing Change DETAILED §8 Assess the Insertion Site
quote:
Assess the Insertion Site
Without touching the site, visually inspect and palpate (through intact skin) for: erythema, swelling, warmth,
induration, tenderness, purulent drainage, or tunnel tract tenderness. Document findings. If signs of infection
are present, complete the dressing change, notify the physician, and document. Do NOT remove the catheter
without a physician order.
title: Assess the Insertion Site

locator: Central Line Dressing Change DETAILED §9 Apply Sterile Gloves
quote:
Apply Sterile Gloves
Don sterile gloves using open or closed glove technique, maintaining sterility throughout. Verify sterile glove
integrity before proceeding. If sterility is compromised, obtain new sterile gloves.
title: Apply Sterile Gloves

locator: Central Line Dressing Change DETAILED §10 Skin Antisepsis with Chlorhexidine Gluconate (CHG)
quote:
Skin Antisepsis with Chlorhexidine Gluconate (CHG)
Open the CHG 2% applicator (ChloraPrep). Apply to insertion site and surrounding skin using a
back-and-forth scrubbing motion for a minimum of 30 seconds. Apply to an area of at least 3–4 cm radius
around the insertion site. Allow to air dry completely — MINIMUM 30 seconds for CHG; do NOT fan, blow, or
blot dry. CHG MUST be completely dry before applying the dressing; wet CHG can cause skin irritation and
reduces efficacy. CHG Allergy/Contraindication: Use 70% isopropyl alcohol scrub × 30 seconds and allow to
dry completely.
title: Skin Antisepsis with Chlorhexidine Gluconate (CHG)

locator: Central Line Dressing Change DETAILED §11 Apply Chlorhexidine-Impregnated Sponge Disk (Biopatch)
quote:
Apply Chlorhexidine-Impregnated Sponge Disk (Biopatch)
Place the Biopatch disk with the CHG-impregnated (blue/darker) side DOWN, directly against the skin at the
catheter insertion site. The disk should lie flat against the skin. Slot the disk around the catheter — do not
force. Replace Biopatch with every dressing change. Contraindications: known CHG allergy, neonates under
7 days, premature infants (skin sensitivity risk).
title: Apply Chlorhexidine-Impregnated Sponge Disk (Biopatch)

locator: Central Line Dressing Change DETAILED §12 Apply Engineered Stabilization Device
quote:
Apply Engineered Stabilization Device
If using a StatLock or similar engineered stabilization device (ESD), apply now per manufacturer instructions.
ESDs are preferred over sutures for catheter stabilization — they reduce catheter movement (which increases
infection and thrombosis risk) without skin puncture. Replace ESD with every dressing change.
title: Apply Engineered Stabilization Device

locator: Central Line Dressing Change DETAILED §13 Apply Transparent Semipermeable Membrane (TSM) Dressing
quote:
Apply Transparent Semipermeable Membrane (TSM) Dressing
Apply the TSM dressing (e.g., Tegaderm CHG, Tegaderm) over the Biopatch and insertion site. Center the
dressing over the insertion site. Apply without tension or stretch (to prevent MARSI — Medical
Adhesive-Related Skin Injury). Press firmly from the center outward to eliminate air bubbles and ensure
complete adhesion. The dressing must be fully occlusive on all edges with no lifting.
title: Apply Transparent Semipermeable Membrane (TSM) Dressing

locator: Central Line Dressing Change DETAILED §14 Secure Catheter Tubing
quote:
Secure Catheter Tubing
Loop excess catheter tubing and secure to the dressing with sterile tape. Ensure catheter hub is accessible
for connection/disconnection. Avoid kinking. Label tubing with catheter type, lumen designation, and change
date per policy.
title: Secure Catheter Tubing

locator: Central Line Dressing Change DETAILED §15 Label the Dressing
quote:
Label the Dressing
Label the dressing with: date of dressing change, time, nurse initials. Place label on the edge of the dressing
— never over the site, as this impairs visualization.
title: Label the Dressing

locator: Central Line Dressing Change DETAILED §16 Remove Gloves and Perform Hand Hygiene
quote:
Remove Gloves and Perform Hand Hygiene
Remove sterile gloves and perform hand hygiene with ABHR immediately after the procedure (WHO Moment
3).
title: Remove Gloves and Perform Hand Hygiene

locator: Central Line Dressing Change DETAILED §17 Dispose of Supplies and Return Environment
quote:
Dispose of Supplies and Return Environment
Dispose of all used supplies per biohazardous waste policy. Remove mask. Return bed to safe position.
Ensure call light is within reach. Perform hand hygiene.
title: Dispose of Supplies and Return Environment

locator: Central Line Dressing Change DETAILED §18 Document in the Medical Record
quote:
Document in the Medical Record
Documentation must include: date/time of dressing change, condition of old dressing, insertion site
assessment findings, antiseptic agent used, dressing type applied, Biopatch applied (yes/no), stabilization
device used, any concerns or complications, and patient tolerance.
title: Document in the Medical Record
